column3: Repeats the focus scene almost verbatim: alleged partners are summoned, do not answer, and punishment is seen.
Directly stages the Day's demand to produce the alleged partners once claimed.
The nearby garden parable supplies regret over associating anyone with the Lord after collapse exposes the error.
Repeats the focus's Day-of-judgment challenge concerning claimed partners.
Pairs humiliation on the Day with the demand to identify the partners defended in rivalry.
Immediately precedes the focus by denying the misleading allies any witness to creation or role as divine support.
Portrays the claimed intercessors as absent and the supposed bond with them as severed.
Immediately opens the judgment sequence in which all are gathered without exception.
Commands the claimants to call those they allege besides God, who cannot remove or redirect harm.
Immediately follows with the criminals seeing the Fire and finding no way to turn away from it.
Shows a gathered judgment scene in which those worshipped are confronted with their claimants.
Immediately establishes the presentation before the Lord and overturns the false denial of the appointed meeting.
Tests alleged partners by summons and denies them ownership, share, and supporting power.
Immediately frames taking Iblis and his progeny as allies instead of God as an evil substitution.
Directly gathers the associators and asks where their alleged partners are.
Immediately supplies the exhaustive record that makes the judgment in the focus accountable and inescapable.
Clarifies the claimed partners as powerless alleged intercessors without divine warrant.
Contrasts answering the Lord with refusal that ends in evil reckoning and Hell.
Within the same surah, rejects taking God's servants as allies and names Hell as the prepared lodging.
The local sequence adds an appointed term for the destruction of unjust communities.
Uses failure to answer a summons as evidence that exclusive divine knowledge and deity are at stake.
Immediately situates the scene among repeated parables and persistent human disputation.
States the prophetic refusal to associate anything with God, supplying the monotheistic counterclaim.
Directly combines the Day's summons for alleged partners with the claimants' admission that no witness remains.
Immediately gives the enclosing Fire and a failed cry for relief, extending the focus's punitive separation.
Shows sinners entering Fire and finding no helpers besides God.
Immediately links rejection of guidance and forgiveness to the arrival of punishment.
The nearby correction, 'I do not associate anyone with my Lord,' directly counters the focus's alleged partnership.
Adds the Day of gathering in which denial of meeting God proves a loss.
Immediately identifies rejection and mockery of warning as the response that precedes the judgment sequence.
Provides the same local surah's construction of a barrier between opposed peoples, a spatial counterpart to the focus's separating mawbiq.
Tests a claimed exclusive alliance with God by demanding a consequence consistent with that claim.
Immediately depicts people who cannot be guided even when called, reinforcing failed response in the local sequence.
Shows associators, under examination, denying that they had ever associated partners with God.
Treats failure to answer a divine challenge as following desire without guidance.
Immediately sets a fixed appointment beyond which the wrongdoers can find no refuge.
Affirms that none shares in God's judgment and that there is no protector besides Him.
Supplies Abraham's explicit dissociation from the associators while turning wholly to the Creator.
Uses a barrier between two groups on the Day; its protective separation contrasts with the focus's destructive separation from false allies.
Directly asks the condemned where the things they used to associate with God are.
Shows the wrongdoer's Day-of-judgment regret over taking the wrong relational path.
Establishes that those joined in wrongdoing share punishment rather than receiving mutual rescue.
Depicts a call across a divinely imposed separation and announces judgment on the wrongdoers.
Rejects taking any protector other than the Creator and closes with a prohibition of association.
Shows disbelievers driven toward the caller on a difficult Day, contrasting the partners' failure to answer the focus's call.
Directly gathers associators with their partners, then separates them as the partners deny being worshipped.
Shows associators identifying their alleged partners only to receive their rejection as liars.
Explicitly challenges those who call beings besides God to summon them and obtain an answer.
States the gravity of associating partners with God and identifies it as a fabricated immense sin.
Adds the Day's interrogation about how people answered the messengers.
Names inherited association as an attempted explanation raised at the time of accountability.
Shows that distress reveals direct dependence on God, while the alleged partners are forgotten.
Returns to the surah's barrier imagery and makes its removal subject to the Lord's true promise.
Adds a Day-of-gathering interrogation in which even messengers defer knowledge to God.
Contrasts the universal response to God's summons on the Day with the false partners' failure to respond.
Directly states that alleged partners neither hear nor answer calls and will repudiate the association on the Day.
Denies that sharing punishment will benefit the wrongdoers, countering any expectation of solidarity among associates.
Shows followers and leaders exchanging blame while standing before their Lord, a judgment-day collapse of false reliance.
Links association with God to exclusion from Paradise, Fire as lodging, and absence of helpers.
Shows a prophet publicly disavowing the gods his people associate with God.
Uses rival, contentious masters to illustrate the incoherence of divided allegiance versus sole devotion.
Shows distress prompting direct return to God, followed by the making of rivals and the stated end in the Fire.
Shows people making partners with God after receiving a gift, supplying a concrete origin of the false association judged in the focus.
Names the fabrication of partners for God from created beings, clarifying the false status of the alleged partners summoned in the focus.
The adjacent contrast between worldly adornment and enduring righteous deeds supplies the evaluative horizon of the local judgment sequence.
Uses the same destruction root for ruin earned through deeds, directly supporting the focus's mawbiq as a destructive consequence.
Affirms God's sole divinity and rejects testimony to additional gods, the doctrinal counterclaim to the focus's alleged partners.
Treats association as a human act under divine sovereignty while denying the messenger a coercive guardianship role.
The surah's earlier designation of worldly adornment as a test provides the broader evaluative frame for its later judgment scenes.
Depicts a genuine, authorized partnership in a divine mission, forming a contrast to powerless and falsely alleged partners.
Establishes a prior acknowledgment of God's lordship for the Day of accountability, contextualizing later association as answerable breach.
Condemns a fabricated kinship between God and jinn and states that those beings will be brought before judgment.
Pairs exclusive worship of God with warning of a great Day, a general but relevant counterpoint to the focus's judgment scene.
